<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par53 />amongst all the forms of Hiphʿîl and Hophʿal, only the {{GHGterm|imperfect}} Hophʿal should have been preserved. A passive of Qal is also indicated in the Tellel-Amarna letters, according to Knudtzon, by a number of imperfect forms, which are undoubtedly due to Canaanite influence, cf. ''Beitr. zur Assyriologie'', iv. 410.<section end=par53 />

<section begin=par54 />{{GHGpar-heading|54|Hithpaʿēl}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|54|a}}
'''1.''' The {{GHGterm|Hithpaʿēl}}<ref>A. Stein, {{GHGcite|title=Der Stamm des Hithpael im Hebr.}} pt. 1, Schwerin, 1893, gives alphabetical statistics of the 1151 forms.</ref> is connected with {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}}, being formed by prefixing to the {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}}-stem (''qaṭṭēl, qaṭṭal'') the syllable {{GHGheb|text=הִתְ}} (Western Aramaic {{GHGheb|text=אִתְ}}, but in Biblical Aramaic {{GHGheb|text=הִתְ}}; Syr. ''’et''<ref>So also in Hebrew {{GHGheb|text=אֶתְחַבַּר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=20|verse=35}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=76|verse=6}} ({{GHGheb|text=אֶשְׁתּוֹלְלוּ}}).</ref>
). Like the preformative {{GHGheb|text=(הִנְ‍) נ‍}} of {{GHGterm|Niphʿal}}, {{GHGheb|text=הִתְ}} has also a reflexive force.

{{GHGmargin-letter|54|b}}
'''2.''' The {{GHGheb|text=ת}} of the prefix in this conjugation, as also in {{GHGterm|Hothpaʿal}} (see h), ''Hithpôēl, Hithpa‛lēl'' and ''Hithpalpel'' (§ 55), under certain circumstances, suffers the following changes:

(''a'') When the stem begins with one of the harder sibilants {{GHGheb|text=ס}}, {{GHGheb|text=צ‍}}, or {{GHGheb|text=ש}}, the {{GHGheb|text=ת}} and the sibilant change places (cf. on this ''metathesis'', {{GHGpar|19|n}}), and at the same time the {{GHGheb|text=ת}} after a {{GHGheb|text=צ‍}} becomes the corresponding emphatic {{GHGheb|text=ט}}: thus {{GHGheb|text=הִשְׁתַּמֵּר|translate=to take heed to oneself}}, for {{GHGheb|text=הִתְשַׁמֵּר}}; {{GHGheb|text=הִסְתַּבֵּל|translate=to become burdensome}}, for {{GHGheb|text=הִתְסַבֵּל}}; {{GHGheb|text=הִצְטַדֵּק|translate=to justify oneself}}, from {{GHGheb|text=צָדַק}}. The only exception is in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=49|verse=3}}, {{GHGheb|text=וְהִתְשׁוֹטַ֫טְנָה}}, to avoid the cacophony of three successive ''t''-sounds.

{{GHGmargin-letter|54|c}}
(''b'') When the stem begins with a ''d''- or ''t''-sound ({{GHGheb|text=ד}}, {{GHGheb|text=ט}}, {{GHGheb|text=ת}}), the {{GHGheb|text=ת}} of the preformative is assimilated to it ({{GHGpar|19|d}}), e.g. {{GHGheb|text=מִדַּבֵּר|translate=speaking, conversing}}; {{GHGheb|text=הִדַּכָּא|translate=to be crushed}}, {{GHGheb|text=הִטַּהֵר|translate=to purify oneself}}, {{GHGheb|text=הִטַּמֵּא|translate=to defile oneself}}, {{GHGheb|text=הִתַּמֵּם|translate=to act uprightly}}. (An exception occurs in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=19|verse=22}}.) The assimilation of the {{GHGheb|text=ת}} occurs also with {{GHGheb|text=נ‍}} and {{GHGheb|text=כ‍}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הִנַּבֵּא|translate=to prophesy}}, as well as {{GHGheb|text=הִתְנַבֵּא}} (cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=24|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=5|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=11|verse=14}}); {{GHGheb|text=תִּכַּוֹנֵן}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=21|verse=27}} (cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=54|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=59|verse=5}}); {{GHGheb|text=תִּכַּסֶּה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=26|verse=26}}; with {{GHGheb|text=שׁ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=7|verse=16}} with {{GHGheb|text=ר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=33|verse=10}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|54|d}}
Rem. Metathesis would likewise be expected, as in the cases under ''b'', when {{GHGheb|text=ת}} and {{GHGheb|text=ז}} come together, as well as a change of {{GHGheb|text=ת}} to {{GHGheb|text=ד}}. Instead of this, in the only instance of the kind ({{GHGheb|text=הִזַּכּוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=1|verse=16}}) the {{GHGheb|text=ת}} is assimilated to the {{GHGheb|text=ז}}, —unless indeed {{GHGheb|text=הִזַּ֫כּוּ}}, {{GHGterm|imperative Niphʿal}} of {{GHGheb|text=זכך}}, is intended.

'''3.''' As in form, so also in meaning, {{GHGterm|Hithpaʿēl}} is primarily (''a'') {{GHGterm|reflexive}} of ''Piēl'', e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הִתְאַזֵּר|translate=to gird oneself}}, {{GHGheb|text=הִתְקַדֵּשׁ|translate=to sanctify oneself}}. Although in these examples the intensive meaning is not distinctly marked, it is so in other cases, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הִתְנַקֵּם|translate=to how oneself revengeful}} (''Niph.'' simply ''to take revenge''), and in the numerous instances where the {{GHGterm|Hithpaʿēl}} expresses ''to make oneself'' that which is predicated by the stem, ''to conduct oneself'' as such, ''to show oneself, to imagine oneself, to ''<section end=par54 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>
